title: IP-SAKTI Sahayak a multilingual, RAG-based (source-cited) AI assistant for Intellectual Property and regulatory guidance in Ayurveda, across national and international regimes.
dataset_link:
The corpus can be assembled from open, authoritative public sources; representative examples:

• Traditional Knowledge Digital Library (TKDL) - tkdl.res.in
• Statutes & rules - India Code, indiacode.nic.in
• IP India public databases (patents/InPASS, trade marks, designs, GI Registry) - ipindia.gov.in
description:
Background:
Ayurveda rests on a vast corpus of codified and community-held traditional knowledge (TK) and on therapeutics derived from plant, microbial and animal sources. Protecting and commercialising an Ayurvedic product means navigating several overlapping regimes at once: patents, geographical indications (GI), trademarks, copyright, designs, trade secrets and plant-variety rights; the Access-and-Benefit-Sharing duties that flow from India’s sovereignty over its biological resources; and the drug-regulatory framework that decides whether a formulation is a classical medicine, a proprietary medicine, a new drug, a phytopharmaceutical, a food or a cosmetic. Practitioners, researchers, AYUSH startups and MSMEs and cultivators routinely struggle with this. The result is twofold: legitimate Ayurvedic innovation is under-protected and under-commercialised, while India’s traditional knowledge remains exposed to misappropriation abroad. Recent shifts - the 2024 patent and biodiversity rules, the WIPO Treaty on Genetic Resources and Associated Traditional Knowledge (2024) and a fast-moving advertising and regulatory landscape - make authoritative, plain-language guidance more necessary than ever, yet no such tool exists for the AYUSH community.
Description:
The assistant answers IPR questions specific to Ayurveda with accuracy, source citation and jurisdictional clarity, keeping the national and the international layers distinct through an explicit jurisdiction switch so that answers are never conflated.
Because intellectual property for an Ayurvedic product is inseparable from how the product is regulated, the assistant first helps classify the formulation. It asks the minimum clarifying questions to determine whether the product is a classical/generic medicine (formulation and method drawn from a First-Schedule authoritative text), a patent-or-proprietary medicine, a new or non-classical drug requiring proof of safety and effectiveness, a phytopharmaceutical, an Ayurveda-Aahar / nutraceutical, or a cosmetic - and then states what each category requires and its very different IP and ABS posture. For example, a classical formulation is largely traditional knowledge that faces the Section 3(p) patenting bar and is defended through the Traditional Knowledge Digital Library, whereas a new drug gains genuine patent potential but must generate clinical evidence.
National coverage spans the Patents Act (and the 2024 Rules), the GI, Trade Marks, Designs, Copyright and Plant-Variety regimes, the Biological Diversity Act (as amended in 2023, with the 2024 Rules) and the allied drug, advertising, labelling and food/cosmetic regimes - the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, the Drugs and Magic Remedies (Objectionable Advertisements) Act and the FSSAI Ayurveda-Aahar regulations. International coverage separately spans TRIPS, the Convention on Biological Diversity and the Nagoya Protocol, the WIPO GRATK Treaty, the PCT, the Madrid and Hague systems, the Budapest Treaty (for micro-organism deposits) and the herbal-product market-access regimes of key export markets.
The assistant also facilitates access to authoritative sources - free official databases directly and the user’s own paid subscriptions only with explicit, logged permission - so that a user can move from a question to the right registry, record or form. It must cite the specific statute, rule, treaty article or record it relies on; clearly state that it provides information and not legal advice; keep its corpus current as the law changes; and never fabricate authority.
Expected solution:
A deployable, multilingual assistant built on retrieval-augmented generation grounded in a curated, version-tracked corpus of statutes, rules, treaties, pharmacopoeial standards, registry records and case law, so that every answer is traceable to a source and hallucination is minimised. The solution should provide: a jurisdiction toggle (India vs international) with the two answer-sets kept visibly separate; routing across IP types together with the formulation-classification flow; an ABS-compliance helper and a TKDL / prior-art pointer; mandatory source citations with a confidence indicator and a path to escalate to a human IP facilitator; multilingual delivery (leveraging national language infrastructure such as Bhashini); and guardrails, a standing 'information, not legal advice' disclaimer and privacy, audit and security aligned to the Digital Personal Data Protection regime and to recognised AI-application standards. A relational knowledge graph and agentic, multi-source orchestration deepen multi-step reasoning and the build can be staged - a citation-grounded retrieval MVP first, then the graph and agentic layers, then paid-source connectors and the full multilingual and voice experience. The output should be evaluable on answer accuracy, citation correctness, safe abstention on out-of-scope or uncertain queries and multilingual quality.
summary: Innovation (3/5): draws on ai applied to a toys & games problem, placing it in the moderate band. Feasibility (3/5): as a software build with moderate integration complexity, a full build is tight for 36 hours and will need scope-cutting. Impact (4/5): reaches a broad public/citizen base within Toys & Games. Tech Depth (5/5): centers on protocol, infrastructure, compliance. Sustainability (3/5): will need a maintenance/upkeep plan post-hackathon. Scalability (4/5): built to extend across states/users with modest rework. Total 22/30 -> Green verdict.

detail.title: IP-SAKTI Sahayak: Multilingual RAG-Based AI Assistant for Ayurveda IP and Regulatory Guidance

overview.in_plain_terms: Build an AI assistant that helps Ayurveda practitioners, researchers, and startups understand the tangled web of patent, trademark, and regulatory rules that apply to their products, with every answer backed by a cited source, not just a confident guess.
overview.why_it_matters: Right now, legitimate Ayurvedic innovation is under-protected because nobody has a clear, authoritative guide through this legal maze, while India's traditional knowledge stays vulnerable to misappropriation abroad. Clear guidance protects both.
pain_points: Ayurvedic IP protection spans overlapping regimes: patents, GI, trademarks, copyright, trade secrets, plant-variety rights, ABS duties, and drug regulation.
Practitioners, researchers, and MSMEs routinely struggle to navigate this complexity.
No authoritative, plain-language guidance tool currently exists for the AYUSH community.
overview.background: Ayurveda's IP landscape is genuinely complex, spanning many overlapping legal regimes, and recent regulatory shifts (2024 patent/biodiversity rules, WIPO TK Treaty) make authoritative guidance more urgent, but no such tool exists.
overview.whats_being_asked: A multilingual, source-cited (RAG-based) AI assistant answering IPR and regulatory questions for the Ayurveda/AYUSH community across national and international regimes.
expected_solution: RAG-based question-answering grounded in real legal/regulatory source documents.
Multilingual support for the AYUSH community.
Source citation for every answer, not black-box responses.
Coverage across multiple overlapping IP and regulatory regimes.

analysis.innovation_scope_note: Moderate. RAG-based Q&A assistants are a well-established pattern by now; the value here is in the domain-specific corpus curation (Ayurveda IP law specifically) and genuine source-citation rigor, not the RAG architecture itself.
analysis.invention_effort_note: High. The RAG architecture itself is achievable, but curating an accurate, comprehensive legal/regulatory corpus across many overlapping regimes is substantial domain research work.

competitive_landscape.note: RAG assistants are common generally, but this specific, deep domain application (Ayurveda IP law) is narrow and requires real legal-domain research most teams won't invest in.

innovation.note: RAG architecture is established; the genuine value and difficulty is in accurate, comprehensive domain corpus curation.

invention.note: Building an accurate knowledge base spanning patents, GI, trademarks, ABS duties, and drug regulation is substantial legal-research effort.

technical_feasibility.tag: Comfortable for the RAG pipeline, Tight for corpus completeness
technical_feasibility.note: RAG implementation itself is well-supported by existing tooling; building a genuinely accurate, comprehensive legal corpus in 36 hours is the harder constraint.

impact_and_benefits.note: Directly helps a specific but real underserved community (AYUSH practitioners/startups) navigate a genuine barrier to innovation.

architecture.note: Document retrieval, generation, and multilingual support in a standard RAG pipeline, well-understood pattern.

overall_verdict.reasoning: Strong pick for a team willing to invest real time in legal/regulatory research rather than treating this as a generic RAG demo. The technical architecture is achievable; differentiation and real value both come from corpus accuracy and citation rigor.

evaluator_lens.biggest_strength: RAG-with-citations is exactly the right architecture for a legal/regulatory guidance tool, this design choice itself shows the PS was written by someone who understands the stakes of getting legal guidance wrong.
evaluator_lens.biggest_risk: Building a generic RAG demo with a thin, inaccurate, or incomplete legal corpus would be actively risky in a domain where wrong guidance has real consequences, corpus quality matters more than usual here.
evaluator_lens.validate_before_commit: Commit real time to sourcing and curating actual Ayurveda IP/regulatory source documents (patent office guidelines, GI registry information, AYUSH drug regulation frameworks) rather than relying on a model's general knowledge dressed up with a citation format.

idea_0_4: Scope your corpus to 2-3 regimes you can research thoroughly (recommend: patents and GI, given their direct relevance to Ayurvedic product protection) rather than attempting full coverage of all named regimes.
Source real regulatory/legal documents for your chosen regimes.
Split: one person on corpus curation, one on the RAG pipeline.
prototype_4_22: Build your document corpus and retrieval index from real sourced documents.
Build the RAG pipeline: retrieval, generation, and citation attachment.
Test that generated answers actually cite the correct source passages, not fabricated or mismatched citations.
integration_22_30: Connect the full Q&A flow with visible source citations for every answer.
Test with genuinely tricky questions that span multiple regimes (e.g. a question touching both patent and GI considerations) to see how the system handles cross-regime complexity.
Add multilingual support for at least one additional language beyond English/Hindi.
polish_30_36: Polish the citation display, users need to be able to actually verify the source, not just see a vague reference.
Rehearse a live Q&A demo with a genuinely complex, realistic AYUSH practitioner question.
Prepare to discuss the corpus's scope limitations honestly, which regimes you covered thoroughly versus not.
build_plan.how_to_stand_out: Ask your system a genuinely hard, realistic question live during the demo, and click through to verify the cited source actually supports the answer, that citation-verification moment is what proves this isn't just a generic chatbot with a legal-sounding prompt.

strengths: RAG-with-citations architecture is exactly right for this domain's stakes, well-matched problem-to-solution fit.
Narrow, specialized domain with low competition from teams unwilling to invest in real legal research.
weaknesses: Full coverage across all named overlapping regimes isn't achievable in 36 hours, requires deliberate scoping.
Corpus accuracy is genuinely high-stakes here, wrong legal guidance has real consequences, this isn't a domain for shortcuts.

team_fit.ideal_ratio: Don't skip dedicated legal research time, this PS's entire credibility rests on corpus accuracy, not just RAG architecture quality.
team_fit.approach: Source and verify real regulatory documents before building the retrieval index, garbage-in-garbage-out applies especially strongly in a legal-guidance context.

ai_buildability_split.ai_can_build_fast: The RAG pipeline architecture itself, retrieval, generation, and citation formatting, all well-supported by existing tooling and patterns.
ai_buildability_split.needs_human_judgment: Verifying that sourced legal/regulatory documents are actually authoritative and current (especially given the PS notes recent 2024 rule changes), and confirming generated answers accurately reflect those sources, not plausible-sounding fabrications.
ai_buildability_split.risk_of_leaning_on_ai_only: A RAG system with a thin or unverified corpus could generate confident-sounding but legally inaccurate guidance, in an IP/regulatory context, that's a genuinely consequential failure mode, not just an embarrassing demo bug.

data_resource_availability.status: Real regulatory documents (patent guidelines, GI registry info, AYUSH regulations) are publicly available from official sources, genuinely accessible for a well-researched corpus, unlike many PS in this batch.
data_resource_availability.backup_plan: If full coverage across all named regimes isn't achievable, scope your corpus explicitly to 2-3 regimes you can source and verify thoroughly, and state that scope limitation clearly rather than implying full coverage.

judge_qna.question: How do you know your system's answers are actually legally accurate, not just plausible-sounding?
judge_qna.strong_answer: Walk through your citation verification process, show a real answer and its cited source side by side, and confirm the source document is authoritative and current, including reflecting the 2024 rule changes mentioned in the PS.
judge_qna.follow_up: What happens when your corpus doesn't have a source for a question, does the system admit uncertainty or fabricate an answer?

judge_qna.question: Why RAG specifically, instead of just fine-tuning a model on legal text?
judge_qna.strong_answer: Point to citation traceability and easier corpus updates as RAG's key advantages here, legal/regulatory information changes, and users in this domain need to verify sources, not just trust a black-box answer.
judge_qna.follow_up: How would you keep the corpus current as regulations continue to evolve?
